news.title: ParaMatildas hunt more Australian football history at World Cup
news.lede: Eloise Northam will be representing the ParaMatildas at her third IFCPF Women's World Cup. (ABC News: Daniel Irvine). The ParaMatildas are looking to defend their IFCPF World Cup title in Atlanta after winning the 2024 tournament. The Pararoos are also searching for a breakthrough top-10 finish in the men's competition.

news.title: Morocco opens museum for Jewish culture in Arab World
news.lede: Local media said the exhibition galleries explore communal institutions, including synagogues, Hebrew schools, and rabbinical courts. The new Museum of Moroccan Jewish Culture opened its doors in the city of Fes on Monday, marking the first time in history that an Arab-Muslim country has allocated public funds to establish a museum entirely dedicated to Jewish culture. According to Morocco's National Foundation of Museums, the 1,700 square meters space invites visitors on a journey into the heart of Moroccan Jewish life and Judaism through a rich and diverse collection of ritual and everyday objects, archaeological, ethnographic and artistic artifacts, archives and rare manuscripts, crafts, traditions, as well as practices and testimonies handed down through the 2500 of Jewish history in the country.

news.title: FIFA to offer members US$6.35 billion development fund windfall
news.lede: FIFA would partly finance its 2026–2030 development fund using reserves built up following a commercially successful 2026 World Cup. PARIS - Football’s world governing body FIFA is planning to set up a US$6.35-billion (S$8 billion) development fund for the next four years, AFP learned on Oct 14 from a source close to the matter. The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Oct 15 in Zurich, where FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the 36 other members of the federation’s executive will gather. To finance this development fund for the 2026–2030 period, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA’s 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.

news.title: Ireland's Women's Football Team To Face Poland In World Cup Bid
news.lede: The Republic of Ireland will face Poland for a place at next year's World Cup in Brazil. Carla Ward's side eased past Kazakhstan in their playoff semi-final last night, winning 12-nil on aggregate. The Girls in Green missed out on qualifying for the 2025 Euros after a playoff defeat to Wales.

news.title: Gianni Infantino faces grilling at potentially ‘explosive’ Fifa council meeting
news.lede: World Cup sell-off, Balogun and peace prize on agenda. Opponents will press home need for independent review. Gianni Infantino will be questioned by Fifa council members over his involvement in the aborted World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair and the decision to award Donald Trump the inaugural Fifa peace prize at what is expected to be a heated meeting at the world governing body’s headquarters on Thursday. The Fifa president rejected repeated calls for an extraordinary general meeting of council in the summer after the emergence of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals, but will meet his critics for the first time since then in Zurich, with one attender predicting that the talks could be “explosive”.

news.title: Fifa to offer extra £2.6bn for football development
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino will be standing for re-election in March. Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn (£2.6bn) increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development across the world. World football's governing body wants to release the money from its reserves in a move which would more than double the level of planned distribution funding for 2027-2030. It says it has been able to release the extra cash because of the commercial success of this summer's World Cup.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Infantino faces FIFA rebels in Zurich after failed World Cup stake sale
news.lede: ZURICH, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Gianni Infantino faces the soccer ⁠leaders who want him gone on Thursday in his first meeting with FIFA’s top brass since his plan to sell a stake in FIFA ⁠tournaments, including the World Cup, collapsed. Infantino has faced calls to resign from the leaders of three regional football confederations – UEFA (Europe), AFC (Asia) and ‌CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) – and their representatives will be present in Zurich for a FIFA Council meeting. They will be joined by their counterparts from Africa, South America and Oceania. On the agenda will be a discussion of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which Infantino was forced to abandon within days of announcing it in July.

news.title: Gianni Infantino faces FIFA rebels in Zurich after failed World Cup stake sale
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has faced calls to resign from the leaders of three regional football confederations. ZURICH – Gianni Infantino faces the football leaders who want him gone on Oct 15 in his first meeting with FIFA’s top brass since his plan to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, collapsed. Infantino has faced calls to resign from the leaders of three regional football confederations – UEFA (Europe), AFC (Asia) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) – and their representatives will be present in Zurich for a FIFA Council meeting. They will be joined by their counterparts from Africa, South America and Oceania.
